clue.text: Actor reflected on the subject of food — plant-based food

parts.note: Sean Bean, or Rowan Atkinson's Mr Bean: an actor's name

indicators.note: something reflected in a mirror is seen back to front, so these words are read in reverse

parts.note: re means concerning, on the subject of
grub is informal for food

explanation.surface: A performer mulls over meals, ending up with a vegetarian dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflected' turns the pair round, making BURGER. Sean Bean or Mr Bean supplies the actor.
explanation.definitionFit: A patty made of beans instead of meat is a vegetarian dish, made from plants.

clue.text: London district heralding extremely inventive musician

indicators.note: heralding means coming before, so this piece goes in front of the next

parts.note: Bow is an area of East London

indicators.note: extremely points to the extreme, outermost letters of the following word

explanation.surface: An East London neighbourhood ushers in a highly creative performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes the outside letters of 'inventive', IE.
explanation.definitionFit: David Bowie was a famously experimental English singer and songwriter.

clue.text: Video game created by American on drugs

parts.note: steroids are drugs, notoriously used by cheating athletes

explanation.surface: A computer game was designed by a doped-up American.
explanation.definitionFit: Asteroids is a classic 1979 Atari arcade title where the player shoots space rocks.

clue.text: Healthcare provider's customers centrally held in automated systems

definitions.note: the name of the chain already ends in s, so the possessive form reads the same

indicators.note: held in says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: bots are automated software programs

indicators.note: centrally picks out the letter at the very middle of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A pharmacy chain's shoppers find themselves dealing with automated systems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centrally' takes O, the middle letter of 'customers'; 'held in' puts it inside BOTS. Boots is a British high-street chemist chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Boots is a major British pharmacy and health retailer, with opticians and hearing services too.

clue.text: Labour policy is something that won't be compromised

parts.note: red is the colour of the UK Labour Party
a line is a policy or official position, as in the party line

explanation.surface: A political party's stance is presented as non-negotiable.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour is Britain's main left-wing party, whose colour is red.
explanation.definitionFit: A red line is a limit or demand a negotiator refuses to give way on.

clue.text: Old sheet covering small area

parts.note: ex means former, old

indicators.note: covering says the sheet goes around the next piece

parts.note: a pane is a sheet of glass

explanation.surface: An antique sheet is spread over a little patch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' wraps the sheet of glass round S, making PANSE.
explanation.definitionFit: An expanse is a wide, open stretch of land, sea or sky.

clue.text: Factory is initially removed to make way for a shopping centre

indicators.note: one letter is taken out so the next takes its place

parts.note: a mill is a factory, such as a cotton mill

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A factory is demolished to clear space for a retail complex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is initially' gives I; it is 'removed to make way for' A in MILL.
explanation.definitionFit: A mall is a large enclosed complex of shops.

clue.text: Nice friends succeeded? Wrong!

parts.note: amis is French for friends, as spoken in Nice
S is an abbreviation for succeeded, used in genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone reacts in alarm: their pals did well? Surely not!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' is the French city, not the adjective, which is why the friends are French.
explanation.definitionFit: Amiss means awry or faulty, so something amiss is something wrong.

clue.text: Navigational craft easily performed last of tasks with it

parts.note: light work is easily done

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of the following word

parts.note: hip and with it both mean fashionable

explanation.surface: A vessel finishes its final duties with ease, staying fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: A lightship is a moored vessel with a beacon, serving as a floating lighthouse to guide shipping.

clue.text: Multi-level shop looked to have a late opening?

parts.note: a store is a shop

indicators.note: an opening that is late is dead and gone, so the first letter is lost

parts.note: eyed means looked at

explanation.surface: A department store considered staying open into the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late' means dead, not after hours: 'to have a late opening' drops the first letter of the word for looked.
explanation.definitionFit: A storeyed building has several floors, each one a level.

clue.text: Expression of frustration about a ring road somewhere in Hertfordshire

indicators.note: about says the first piece goes round the next

parts.note: WTF is the texting shorthand for an exasperated outburst
a ring is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: A driver swears at a ring road somewhere in an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A inside WTF. Hertfordshire is a county just north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Watford is a large town in Hertfordshire, north-west of London.

clue.text: President taking time with good shots on the green

indicators.note: taking means taking in, so the president holds the next piece

parts.note: Vladimir Putin, the Russian president

explanation.surface: A head of state takes his time playing fine golf shots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' puts T inside PUTIN to give PUTTIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting is striking the golf ball gently towards the hole on the smooth grass around it.

clue.text: Going back, headed for an exit

indicators.note: headed here means beheaded, losing the first letter

parts.note: regression is the act of going back

explanation.surface: Someone retreats, making for the door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'headed' looks like 'heading towards', but it means the word loses its head, R.
explanation.definitionFit: Egression is a formal word for going out, the act of leaving.

clue.text: Doctor tries another examination

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A doctor attempts one more medical check-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' is a verb meaning tamper with, not a physician; it rearranges 'tries'.
explanation.definitionFit: A resit is a second attempt at a failed exam.

clue.text: Sounds beginning at the left part of the mouth

indicators.note: the letter at the left of a written word is its first

parts.note: the lips frame the mouth

explanation.surface: Noises start up from the left side of someone's mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning' is not an indicator but the word to pick from: 'at the left' takes its B.
explanation.definitionFit: Blips are short high-pitched electronic beeps, as on a radar screen.

clue.text: Action on course to promote change in voting habits

parts.note: to back something is to support or promote it
a swing is a shift in voter support between parties

explanation.surface: A campaign aims to encourage voters to switch allegiance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' is a golf course, not a plan of action.
explanation.definitionFit: A backswing is the golfer's motion of drawing the club back before striking.

clue.text: Satirical, lively Scotsman

parts.note: swift means quick, lively
Ian is a typically Scottish first name

explanation.surface: A spirited man from Scotland has a mocking wit.
explanation.definitionFit: Jonathan Swift wrote Gulliver's Travels and A Modest Proposal; his style is the byword for biting satire.

clue.text: Completely and remarkably weird niche trousers

indicators.note: used as a verb: to trouser is to pocket, so one piece takes in the other
something weird is odd and out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: remarkably and very both mean extremely

explanation.surface: Some unusual, specialist trousers are thoroughly odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weird' rearranges 'niche' to EINCH; 'trousers' is a verb: it takes in VERY after the E.
explanation.definitionFit: Every inch is an idiom meaning wholly, in every respect: every inch a king.

clue.text: Storage facility set up outside back of arena

indicators.note: outside means this piece goes around the next
in a down entry, up means the letters are written bottom to top

parts.note: a TV is a set, the television

indicators.note: back of points to the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A storage depot is built around the rear of a stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' reverses TV to VT; 'outside' puts it round A, the end of 'arena'.
explanation.definitionFit: A vat is a large tank for holding liquids such as beer or dye.

clue.text: Heads of campus halls worked with uni and LGBT music venue

indicators.note: worked means shaped or kneaded, so these letters are reworked
heads of picks the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: University hall leaders teamed up with the student body and an LGBT society on a dance venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked' rearranges CH, UNI and LGBT together.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightclub is a late-opening venue for dancing to music.

clue.text: Criticise players in front of international fans who've paid to watch

indicators.note: in front of places this piece before the next

parts.note: the cast are the players in a show
the gate is the paying crowd at a sports match

explanation.surface: Actors berate a crowd of international supporters who have bought tickets.
explanation.definitionFit: To castigate is to reprimand severely, a strong form of criticism.

clue.text: One skilled amateur trains frantically

indicators.note: frantically suggests wild disorder, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A capable hobbyist practises in a frenzy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frantically' rearranges 'trains' to RTISAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An artisan is a craftsperson, a skilled manual worker.

clue.text: Bloke got ripped, partly as a morale booster

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A man getting muscular feels his confidence lifted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partly' points to blokE GOT RIPped.
explanation.definitionFit: An ego trip is something done chiefly to boost one's self-esteem or sense of importance.

clue.text: Uncover extremes of in-fighting hidden by party

indicators.note: hidden by says the letters are tucked inside the next piece

parts.note: the DUP is Northern Ireland's Democratic Unionist Party

indicators.note: extremes of takes the outermost letters of the following word

explanation.surface: A party conceals the worst of its internal feuding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremes of' takes the outer letters of 'in-fighting'; 'hidden by' tucks them inside Northern Ireland's Democratic Unionist Party.
explanation.definitionFit: To dig up a secret is to bring it to light, exposing it.

clue.text: Tobacco in tin used up

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
out means exhausted, all used up

explanation.surface: The tobacco tin has been emptied.
explanation.walkthrough: Snout is British prison slang for tobacco.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, especially in prisons, snout means tobacco or a cigarette.

clue.text: Leader ousted from one-time car plant

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter, and it is thrown out

parts.note: Morris was a British car marque, now defunct

explanation.surface: A boss is pushed out of a former car factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'car plant' looks like a factory, but 'plant' is the definition; 'Leader ousted from' drops M.
explanation.definitionFit: Orris is a kind of iris, grown for its fragrant root.

clue.text: Vehicle travelling east (not south) or west

indicators.note: travelling suggests moving about, so the letters are shuffled
not says the following letter is left out

explanation.surface: A car is driving eastward, or not, perhaps westward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' drops S from 'east' to leave EAT; 'travelling' rearranges EAT + OR + WEST.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-seater is a car, plane or similar with room for only two people.

clue.text: Little fish always grabs line

indicators.note: grabs says the first piece takes hold of the next inside it

parts.note: ever means always, as in ever hopeful

explanation.surface: A tiny fish keeps snatching at a fishing line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grabs' puts L inside EVER.
explanation.definitionFit: An elver is a young eel, a small fish.

clue.text: Former New York official smuggling diamonds? Damn!

indicators.note: smuggling means carrying inside, so this piece holds the next

parts.note: Rudy Giuliani was formerly mayor of New York
D is the abbreviation for diamonds in card games

explanation.surface: An ex-mayor caught smuggling jewels? Blast!
explanation.walkthrough: 'smuggling' puts D inside RUDY.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruddy is a mild British euphemism for bloody, used as an expletive.

clue.text: Advances in marketing of Japanese medical kit?

parts.note: an inro is a small traditional Japanese case that hangs from the sash, often holding medicines
ads are marketing material

explanation.surface: A firm makes progress selling Japanese first-aid supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: The parts run in answer order: marketing (ADS) of the inro comes after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Inroads are gains made into a territory or market, progress forward.

clue.text: On retirement, give a speech that's hated

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the word is turned backwards

parts.note: to deliver an address is to give a speech

explanation.surface: A retiring figure makes a farewell address that people loathe.
explanation.definitionFit: Reviled means fiercely criticised and despised, close to hated.

clue.text: The crux of marrying is trust

indicators.note: of here means taken from within, so the answer lies inside the next words

explanation.surface: A homily states that faith is the essence of a marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The crux of' reads as the definition then the hidden signal: marryinG IS Trust.
explanation.definitionFit: The gist is the essential point or substance of something.

clue.text: Broadcast on iPlayer buffers at the start, with no means of being fixed

definitions.text: with no means of being fixed

indicators.note: broadcast also means scattered, as seeds are sown, so the letters are scattered
at the start picks the opening letter of the word it follows

explanation.surface: A programme on the BBC streaming service keeps buffering at the start and cannot be repaired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' rearranges ON, IPLAYER and B together. iPlayer is the BBC's online streaming service.
explanation.definitionFit: Inoperably means in a way that cannot be operated on or put right.
